title: WPSS/986/2024 of ATUL SHANKAR RANA Vs SECRETARY AYUSH AND AYUSH SHIKSHA

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
14.06.2024 WPSS No. 986 of 2024
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Vijay Khanduri, learned counsel for the
petitioner.
2. Mr. Narayan Dutt, learned Standing Counsel
for the State.
3. By means of this writ petition, the petitioner
has challenged the impugned order dated 08.06.2024
(Annexure No. 1 to the writ petition) passed by the
respondent no. 2/Director, Ayurvedic and Unani
Services, Uttarakhand, Dehradun, whereby the
petitioner, who is working with the respondent no. 2
as a pharmacist, has been transferred from
Government Ayurvedic Hospital, Bidhauli, District
Dehradun to Ayushman Arogya Mandir,
Chhadandev, District Pithoragarh.
4. It is contended by the learned counsel for the
petitioner that the petitioner is posted at Government
Ayurvedic Hospital, Bidhauli, District Dehradun
since 2014, which is an accessible place and now he
has been transferred to Ayushman Arogya Mandir,
Chhadandev, District Pithoragarh under the
Uttarakhand Annual Transfer for Public Servants
Act, 2017 (hereinafter referred as the Annual
Transfer Act, 2017).
5. Petitioner moved a representation dated
01.05.2024 before his transfer to the respondent no.
2/Director, Ayurvedic and Unani Services,
Uttarakhand, Dehradun stating therein that both
kidneys of father of the petitioner were damaged and
his father has had his kidney transplant and for that
reason, petitioner has to visit B.L.K. Max Hospital,
Delhi regularly and need to be extra cautious. Due to
which, petitioner has requested the respondent no. 2

to exempt the petitioner from being transferred in
this transfer season. The said representation has not
been considered.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn
the attention of this Court to Section 3(d) of the
Annual Transfer Act, wherein serious patient has
been defined and which includes the parents of the
Government Servant.
7. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the
petitioner that in view of the provisions of Section
3(d) and 7(d)(iii) of the Annual Transfer Act,
wherein exemption is given to such category of
persons, who are serious patient.
8. The petitioner has annexed the medical
certificate issued by B.L.K. Max Hospital, Delhi of
his father, which reflects that his father has already
undergone one kidney transplant from the kidney of
mother of the petitioner.
9. Petitioner has also annexed the document as
Annexure No. 3 to the writ petition, wherefrom it is
clear that petitioner's father is a renal patient and he
had undergone the kidney transplant.
10. In view of the above peculiar facts and
circumstances, the writ petition is, therefore,
disposed of with a direction to the respondent no.
2/Director, Ayurvedic and Unani Services,
Uttarakhand, Dehradun to decide the representation
dated 01.05.2024 (Annexure No. 4 to the writ
petition) by a speaking and reasoned order within a
period of four weeks from the production of certified
copy of this order.
11. Meanwhile, the impugned transfer order dated
08.06.2024 qua the petitioner shall remain stayed.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 14.06.2024
Akash
